More Britons believe that multiculturalism makes the country worse - not better

Multi-culturalism is great, when your adding cultures that harmonize with existing notions and integrate easily. When you add cultures into the mix that vehemently oppose preconceived notions and actively undo multi-cultural efforts then all you get is friction. With friction you get pain and anger from the communities that find their values torn apart.

This works well for the current government though, people are so mad at each other for their opposing views on modesty, sexuality and religious values (all of which are personal and have little impact on other people's lives unless actively forced) that the government can get up to all the shady shit it wants to because the media, news networks and everyday discussion is filled with talk about "us" versus "them" rhetoric and arguments about rights and values even while the government spends their time dismantling individual rights and community powers while cutting budgets left and right to preserve their own incomes.

For an example: If you own a gun in the UK; which you are allowed to do if it's licensed even if it's expensive to get the firearm and expensive to get it licensed; the police can conduct inspections of your firearms at any time with no notice even if you aren't present. This law that was put in quietly about 3 years ago basically allows any property with a registered firearm to be entered without consent at any time by the police. If you resist or otherwise make it hard to inspect the firearm you can be arrested and fined heavily, along with getting your license revoked and your firearm impounded pending a court hearing which you are not allowed to speak at and then your firearm is confiscated as it is treated as unlicensed.

You'll hear about ISIS throwing a few gay men off a tower a thousand miles away a million times in the newspapers before you hear about this law. A law of dozens of similar laws which give the police massive amounts of control and provisions for extreme violence if they deem it needed up to and including artillery strikes. I'm not even kidding there.

Not to mention the privacy laws which have made private information the property of the government by law, if a company has your email they need to give it to MI5, if a company has your address they need to give it to MI5, if a shop sells you size 3 shoes for your child they are required by law to make that information available to MI5.

You'll hear warnings from pundits and government officials that we need to fight against sharia law taking root in our country, and I agree there. But maybe the government officials saying this should take a look at the shambles and rags that are laws now are. I mean we have non-police speed catchers sitting on blind junctions to catch people going over the limit, we have actual bounty hunters setting out to catch people to make money off the fines levied. I know this because I challenged one of these a while ago and they didn't even take it to court, the reason was that I questioned if a non-police operative could bring such a charge against me, they dropped the charge and the fine. But you can guarantee that law is on the table somewhere to get changed too.
